items.title: Morning, Day and Evening, Night
items.medium: Serigraphs with embossing and foil stamping, a matched pair, each hand-signed, edition 182/300
items.size: Image about 38 × 28½ in; framed about 4 ft tall each
description: Very large! 4ft tall each framed.
Overview

Up for acquisition is the quintessential two-piece suite from the "Father of Art Deco," Romain de Tirtoff (Erté), usually retailing at $20,000 for the set. This set features his world-renowned masterpieces "Morning, Day" and "Evening, Night," produced in 1982-1985.

Both pieces are hand-signed by the artist and share the matching limited edition number 182/300. This primary edition is highly coveted for its vibrant colors, intricate embossing, and luxurious foil stamping on heavy black wove paper.
Item Specifics
• Artist: Erté (Romain de Tirtoff)
• Title: Morning, Day / Evening, Night (2-Piece Suite)
• Medium: Mixed Media Serigraph with Embossing and Foil Stamping
• Edition Number: 182/300 (Matching Pair)
• Signature: Hand-signed by Erté in pencil (Lower Right)
• Year of Production: 1982–1985
• Image Dimensions: Approx. 38” x 28.5”
• Paper: Premium Heavyweight Black Wove Paper

These pieces have been kept in a climate-controlled, smoke-free environment and are in Excellent condition. The colors remain remarkably vibrant with no signs of fading or foxing. The foil stamping is crisp and intact.
Why This Suite?

The "Morning/Evening" suite is widely considered one of Erté’s most iconic visual narratives. While individual prints from later, larger editions appear frequently, a matching numbered set from the limited 300-run is a blue-chip addition to any serious Art Deco collection.
Shipping & Handling
Due to the value and size of these works, shipping will be handled with extreme care:
• Professional Packing: Artwork will be packed using acid-free materials and heavy-duty art shippers.
• Insurance: Full-value insurance is included in the shipping cost.
• Signature Required: Delivery will require an adult signature upon arrival.
Authenticity Guaranteed
I stand behind the authenticity of this suite. The signatures and edition numbers are clear and consistent with Erté’s verified works from this period.
** the actual prints are in mint condition. The frames have some scuffs, but not too bad. Will send pictures if desired.
Pick up only unless offers to pay for professional art shipping.

items.title: Two Geese
items.medium: Woodblock print, ō-tanzaku format, signed Koson with seal
description: *would prefer to ship without frame for safety, but this can be discussed if frame is desired*

Up for sale is a stunning authentic Japanese woodblock print (moku-hanga) by the renowned artist Ohara Koson (1877–1945). This piece belongs to the kacho-e (bird-and-flower) genre and dates to the early part of the artist’s career, approximately circa 1910.
Artistic Details
• Artist: Ohara Koson (Signed "Koson" with the artist's circular seal).
• Subject: Two Chinese Geese.
• Format: O-tanzaku (Large vertical format).
• Period: Late Meiji / Early Taisho Era (c. 1900–1912).
• Technique: Woodblock print on paper with beautiful graduation (bokashi) in the background.
Signature & Authentication

This print features the early "Koson" signature and the circular artist seal. This is a crucial distinction for collectors, as it marks his early period of work before he changed his art name to "Shoson" in 1926.
Condition Report
• Authenticity: Guaranteed original woodblock print, not a modern digital reproduction.
• Surface: The print shows characteristic "foxing" (age-related brown spotting) and some general toning/darkening to the paper, which is common for a piece of this age.
• Color: The pigments remain well-defined, particularly the fine line work on the feathers and the yellow-orange of the beaks and feet.
• Please review the high-resolution photos carefully as they form part of the condition description.
Provenance & Shipping
This is a beautiful example of Shin-hanga era artistry, perfect for collectors of Japanese nature prints or admirers of Koson's masterful bird studies.
• Shipping: Will be shipped flat and securely between heavy-duty acid-free boards to ensure safe arrival.

items.title: Gilded Picture Frame
items.medium: Gilt wood with beaded inner lip, original maker's label
description: Antique Ben J. Cueny Detroit Gold Gilt Wood Frame – 40" x 25"
Provenance & History:

This is an authentic early 20th-century picture frame handcrafted by the renowned Ben J. Cueny of Detroit, Michigan. The original paper label is still attached to the reverse, bearing his historic 1420 Brush St. address. Cueny was a staple of the Detroit art scene from the 1920s through the 1940s, known for providing high-end custom framing for prominent local artists and collectors. So this frame is estimated to be made during that period, and the aged look on it confirms this (heavier, darker wood, aged paper on back).
Design & Aesthetic:
• Style: A beautiful blend of Art Deco and Neoclassical Revival.
• Finish: Original gold gilt/leaf finish with a rich, age-appropriate patina.
• Detailing: Features a sophisticated beaded inner lip and a tiered profile that adds depth and "window" effect to any artwork.
Condition:

Excellent vintage condition. Unlike many frames of this era, the gesso and gilt are remarkably intact. There is very minor shelf wear consistent with age, which only adds to its authentic antique character. It is structurally sound and ready for a canvas or mirror.
Dimensions:
• Outer Dimensions: 40.5 x 25.5
• Inner/Rabbet Size (Fits Artwork): 21 3/16 x 36 1/4
Shipping & Handling:
Due to the significant size and delicate nature of this antique, it will be professionally packed and insured. Also available for local pickup in the Lynchburg, VA area.

items.medium: Painting on canvas, signed and dated, in a vintage gilt-tone frame
description: Beautiful signed and dated original portrait by Betsy Flagg Melcher (1900–1991), depicting two young children seated together in a charming, softly rendered interior portrait.
